issues.title: Missing adjoint in the normal-equation pseudoinverse formula
issues.failure_explanation: For A:H^n-to-H^m in the paper's notation, (A^*A)^dagger is an n-by-n classical matrix, while the final factor needed to obtain an operator H^m-to-F^n is A^*. Multiplication by A as printed is not even dimensionally defined for a general rectangular Bochner matrix. With the adjoint inserted, the SVD calculation gives V Sigma^{-1} U^*, exactly as claimed elsewhere.
issues.overall_effect: Item 1 of the pseudoinverse lemma is malformed, but the paper's primary pseudoinverse theorem and subsequent uses employ the correct SVD operator. No later formal result depends on the missing-adjoint form.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the terminal A by A* in item 1 and in its matching SVD calculation, yielding A† = (A*A)†A*. This gives a well-typed map from H^m to F^n and equals VΣ^{-1}U*; no downstream statement needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: Dimensional typing and the old SVD pseudoinverse theorem uniquely force the adjoint, and the displayed calculation already implicitly uses it. No inference or construction must be changed, so the defect is transcriptional.

issues.title: False reverse-order pseudoinverse law for an arbitrary middle factor

failure_location.quote: \item If $\Matrix{B} \in \F^{k \times m}$ has full column rank and $\Matrix{C} \in \F^{n \times l}$ has full row rank, $(\Matrix{B} \Batrix{A} \Matrix{C})^\pinv = \Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated full-column/full-row assumptions on the outer factors do not make the reverse-order law valid for an arbitrary middle factor. For the admissible real example A=[1,0]^T, B=[[1,0],[1,1]], and C=[1], B and C have the required ranks, but (BAC)^dagger=[1/2,1/2], whereas C^dagger A^dagger B^dagger=[1,0]. Thus the claimed direct substitution fails the self-adjoint Penrose conditions.
issues.overall_effect: Item 2 of the pseudoinverse lemma is false at its advertised generality. Later cross-factorization arguments need only the valid special case of a full-column factor followed by a full-row factor, so no later formal result requires the false unrestricted law.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the reverse-order identity only under valid compatibility assumptions, for example requiring B*B to commute with AA† and CC* to commute with A†A in addition to the stated rank assumptions, and verify all four Penrose equations. State as a corollary the valid case (XC)† = C†X† for a full-column-rank Bochner matrix X followed by a full-row-rank classical matrix C, which is the case needed later.
issues.why_classification: The counterexample rules out the advertised law for generic full-rank outer factors. A comparable reverse-order law and every later use survive through a contained Penrose-equation argument, but the necessary compatibility conditions exclude a natural class of full-rank factors and therefore constitute meaningful scope loss beyond a minor repair. No global reconstruction or major loss is required.

issues.title: HOSVD theorem admits an input for which its SVDs are undefined

failure_location.quote: For $\Batrix{A} \in \Hilb^{m \times n}$, let $\Batrix{A} = \Batrix{U} \Matrix{\Sigma} \Matrix{V}^\ast$ and $\Batrix{A}^\trans = \Batrix{P} \Matrix{\Lambda} \Matrix{Q}^\ast$ be SVDs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By definition, an SVD of a Bochner matrix corresponds to a compact SVD of a usual matrix and is not defined when the Bochner matrix is identically zero.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem quantifies over every Bochner matrix A, including A=0, but its construction begins by choosing SVDs of A and A^T. The old SVD theorem assumes a nonzero matrix, and the following old remark explicitly says that an SVD is not defined for the identically zero Bochner matrix. Hence the HOSVD construction is undefined on an allowed input.
issues.overall_effect: The HOSVD theorem is well-defined only for nonzero inputs under the paper's own convention. Its proof and all positive-rank approximation claims remain valid after that restriction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis A ≠ 0 to the HOSVD theorem before choosing the two SVDs. The zero matrix may be noted separately as having the zero approximant and trivial rank and error conclusions, without invoking an SVD.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine missing input qualification because the paper explicitly leaves the zero-matrix SVD undefined. The defect concerns only the exceptional zero case and is resolved by a routine local hypothesis or case split without changing the method, estimate, or positive-rank regime.

issues.title: Undefined residual-row variable in ABCD
issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm samples i_s but then evaluates R(i,j), where i has no value anywhere in the procedure. Hence the starting column cannot be computed as printed. Replacing i by i_s makes the instruction well-defined and matches the immediately preceding assignment and the analogous usual-ACA step.
issues.overall_effect: ABCD is not executable as printed, and ABCDX and the numerical experiments that invoke it inherit that failure. No formal theorem depends on the malformed variable name.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace R(i,j) by R(i_s,j) in the starting-column maximization of ABCD. The resulting instruction uses the row sampled immediately beforehand and makes ABCD, ABCDX, and their experimental invocations executable.
issues.why_classification: The immediately preceding assignment of i_s and the analogous classical ACA step uniquely determine the intended index. Correcting that single identifier requires no change to the algorithmic reasoning or guarantee.

issues.title: Wrong operator sign makes the stated BVP family resonant

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In our experiment, we choose $\alpha_{\max} = \beta_{\max} = 2$, $m = n = 100$, and $K = 75$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed operator sends sin(kx) to (k^2-alpha^2)sin(kx), while the immediately following claimed coefficient uses k^2+alpha^2. Under the literal minus sign, alpha=1 and alpha=2 are Dirichlet eigenvalues; at those parameters generic right-hand sides have no solution and compatible right-hand sides are nonunique. This contradicts the asserted solution map on the subsequently chosen full interval alpha in [0,2]. Changing the second minus sign to plus simultaneously matches the alpha factor and removes those resonances.
issues.overall_effect: Under the literal equation, the advertised solution map on the stated parameter rectangle is not well-defined and the associated numerical experiment cannot represent that BVP. The independent beta-coefficient typo remains the C04 root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the boundary-value problem to -u'' + α^2u = cos(βx), retaining the stated parameter rectangle, grids, and the coefficient factor k^2+α^2. This removes the Dirichlet resonances and requires no alpha-related recomputation of the sampled map.
issues.why_classification: The old source uniquely forces the plus sign: its coefficients use k^2+α^2, while the advertised interval includes α=1 and α=2, where the literal minus-sign problem does not define the claimed solution map. The existing construction already uses the plus-sign alpha dependence, so one transcriptional sign correction resolves this root without rebuilding the experiment.

issues.title: Wrong forcing-parameter factor in the Fourier coefficients
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the displayed series solves the supplied boundary-value problem. Directly projecting the supplied forcing cos(beta x) onto sin(kx) gives k[1-(-1)^k cos(beta pi)]/(k^2-beta^2), with the integer cases understood by continuity. The old coefficient instead contains k^2+beta^2. Thus the asserted solution series differs from the one implied by the stated forcing and generally does not solve the displayed problem.
issues.overall_effect: The sampled solution map and the reported approximation errors for this experiment generally correspond to incorrect Fourier coefficients. No formal theorem elsewhere in the paper depends on the experiment.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the forcing-dependent factor k^2+β^2 by k^2-β^2, so that u_k = k[1-(-1)^k cos(βπ)]/((k^2+α^2)(k^2-β^2)), with the removable cases β=k evaluated by continuity. Regenerate the sampled Bochner matrices, rerun all four approximation methods, and replace the reported errors, figure, and associated numerical discussion with the corrected results.
issues.why_classification: Although the algebraic correction is local, the published numerical data and comparisons were formed from the wrong solution map, so a one-symbol edit does not repair the affected chain. Recomputing and updating this single experiment is contained and preserves the same BVP, algorithms, domains, and comparison objective, but it is nontrivial work exceeding a minor repair and does not require global proof reconstruction.

issues.title: Unsupported zero-round rook-pivoting behavior in the numerical experiment

failure_location.quote: When $n_{\mathrm{rook}} = 0$, the rows are selected at random and the choice of columns is adaptive.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that at n_rook=0 the rows are random and the columns adaptive. The printed rook and ABCD contracts actually allow only n_rook in N, and the rook routine assigns i_* only inside its loop. If the routine is nevertheless executed with zero rounds, the loop is skipped and no row index is returned. Consequently, the printed algorithms do not establish the claimed zero-round behavior or a reproducible zero-round numerical regime.
issues.overall_effect: The zero-round ABCD/ABCDX experiments and their qualitative interpretation are not executable from the old pseudocode as printed. Positive-round behavior and the paper's formal results are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Allow n_rook=0 in the ABCD and ABCDX contracts and guard the call to the positive-round rook routine. When n_rook=0, retain the already computed pair consisting of the random row i_s and its adaptively selected column j_s; when n_rook>0, call rook exactly as before.
issues.why_classification: The skipped loop leaves an output uninitialized, so this is not merely a misspelled identifier. Nevertheless, the preceding ABCD instructions and the experiment's prose already specify the intended zero-round pair, and one local control-flow branch makes that advertised regime executable without changing positive-round behavior, the method, or any guarantee.
